_comment: STT backends for the audio lane of the segment-time benchmark. Three orthogonal axes per entry: (1) supported_hardware — explicit list of hardware-class keys from reference.json, or ['*'] for any class; the harness refuses to RTF-capture on a class outside this list. (2) fallback — production runtime behavior, 'use this if the preferred provider is unavailable'. (3) benchmarkable — whether the harness should run RTF capture; cloud backends are not benchmarkable in the RTF sense (network noise dominates) and use a flat wall_seconds_per_5min rule of thumb instead. Solstone supports two in-process ASR backends (parakeet via CoreML/ONNX, whisper via faster-whisper); both are libraries inside the Solstone Python process. parakeet-nim was investigated and explicitly deferred — see the project's Transcription Backend Architecture doc. RTF entries populated by `python -m think.benchmark.harness --transcriber <id> --audio-fixture <path> --class <hw>`.

parakeet.label: Parakeet TDT (in-process: CoreML / linux-x86_64 ONNX)
parakeet.notes: In-process backend (observe/transcribe/parakeet.py): CoreML helper on macOS Apple Silicon, onnx-asr + onnxruntime on linux-x86_64. Does NOT run on linux/aarch64 (DGX Spark) — those hosts use whisper.

whisper.label: Whisper (faster-whisper, in-process)
whisper.notes: Cross-platform in-process backend. Universal floor: runs anywhere Python runs, including linux/aarch64 (DGX Spark). Used as the production fallback when the preferred provider is unavailable, and as the Spark default since the in-process parakeet path doesn't cover aarch64.

gemini.label: Gemini (cloud)
gemini.notes: Cloud backend with diarization. Wall-clock is network-bound; the flat wall_seconds_per_5min is a rule-of-thumb baseline, not a hardware-derived measurement. Not benchmarkable in the RTF sense.

revai.label: Rev.ai (cloud)
revai.notes: Cloud backend with diarization. Wall-clock includes provider-side queueing that varies by 2-3x; treat as a rough estimate. Not benchmarkable in the RTF sense.
